# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.
- Transactions: `govern: [ transaction ]` on steps, not `@Transactional`.
- Errors: a handler YAML in `officefloor/escalation/`, not `@ControllerAdvice`.

### Worked example — `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`

The whole shape of an endpoint. The sections after this one are the reference.

`src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml`

```yaml
# First step runs first. Validate before Load so an invalid body is a 400,
# not masked by a 404 for a missing owner.
validate:
  class: com.example.owner.ValidateOwner
  next: load
load:
  class: com.example.owner.LoadOwner
  next: apply
apply:
  class: com.example.owner.ApplyOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: save
save:
  class: com.example.owner.SaveOwner
  govern: [ transaction ]
  next: respond
respond:
  class: com.example.owner.RespondWithOwner
```

```java
// One public method each. State moves by Out<T> (set) → @Val (read), matched by type.
public class ValidateOwner {
  public void validate(@RequestBody @Valid OwnerRequest request, Out<OwnerRequest> body) {
    body.set(request); // body read once here; republished for later steps
  }
}
public class LoadOwner {
  public void load(@PathVariable("ownerId") int ownerId, OwnerRepository repository,
      Out<Owner> ownerOut) throws OwnerNotFoundException {
    Owner owner = repository.findById(ownerId);
    if (owner == null) throw new OwnerNotFoundException(ownerId); // handled below
    ownerOut.set(owner);
  }
}
public class ApplyOwner { // @Val yields the stored object, not a copy — mutate in place
  public void apply(@Val OwnerRequest request, @Val Owner owner) {
    owner.setFirstName(request.firstName());
    owner.setLastName(request.lastName());
  }
}
public class SaveOwner {
  public void save(@Val Owner owner, OwnerRepository repository) {
    repository.save(owner);
  }
}
public class RespondWithOwner {
  public void respond(@Val Owner owner, ObjectResponse<OwnerResponse> response) {
    response.send(OwnerResponse.from(owner)); // this step responds; 200 by default
  }
}
```

`src/main/resources/officefloor/escalation/com.example.owner.OwnerNotFoundException.yml`

```yaml
handle:
  class: com.example.owner.HandleOwnerNotFound
```

```java
public class HandleOwnerNotFound {
  public void handle(@Parameter OwnerNotFoundException ex,
      ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<String>> response) {
    response.send(new ResponseEntity<>(ex.getMessage(), HttpStatus.NOT_FOUND));
  }
}
```

### Step wiring

Each top-level YAML entry is a developer-chosen step name; the first is the entry
point. `class:` names the function. **Give each function class exactly one public
method** — several public methods fail at start-up unless every reference adds
`method:`.

- `next: <step>` — run that step afterwards. This step's return value arrives there
  as `@Parameter T`.
- `outputs: { <name>: <step> }` — conditional branches. Declare a
  `@FunctionalInterface` parameter annotated `@Flow("<name>")` and call it to take the
  branch; not calling it short-circuits.

### Function parameters

Declare only what the step needs; they resolve by role:

- `@PathVariable`, `@RequestParam`, `@RequestBody` — Spring MVC annotations work.
- Spring beans (repositories, mappers, services) — injected by type as normal.
- `ObjectResponse<T>` (`net.officefloor.web.ObjectResponse`) — send the response with
  `response.send(dto)`. This is how a step responds; wrap as
  `ObjectResponse<ResponseEntity<T>>` to set status explicitly.
- `@Parameter T` (`net.officefloor.plugin.section.clazz.Parameter`) — the previous
  step's return value, a `@Flow` argument, or a thrown escalation.

### Passing state between steps — `Out<T>` / `@Val`

Steps do not call each other. Beyond the single `@Parameter` hand-off, publish state
into a variable (`net.officefloor.plugin.variable`):

- Producer declares `Out<T>` and calls `set(...)`; consumer declares `@Val T`.
- Matching is **by type** — two variables of the same type in one pipeline need a
  `@Qualifier` annotation to disambiguate.

Each is settled as settling it alone would (one going to PENDING counts as settled), in one transaction: if any is refused (or the user is a viewer, or the sheet archived), none is settled, all count as refused and nothing is stored or recorded. Otherwise they form the sheet's next settle batch, recorded after the claims' own lines as BATCH_SETTLED batch=<n> count=<claims> total=<their SETTLED frozen figures added up>. Responds {settled, refused, last}. The step owns its transaction, so it is not governed here. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/comments — comment on a claim. Body {"text":"..."}, kept trimmed with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today. Refused with 422 for an empty comment; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/date — a steward re-dates an OPEN or PENDING claim. Body {"date":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. Its due-by and any statement figure stay, and so its period (the one its due-by falls in) and its number. Refused with 422 for anyone but a steward, any other status, a date after its person's retirement, or a claim due by a date in a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/defer — defer an OPEN claim to a date after the sheet's today. Body {"until":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. Until the sheet's today reaches it the claim counts in no total, is not overdue, cannot be settled and is left unbound by a statement. Refused with 422 for a claim not OPEN, a date not after today, or a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/due-by — a steward sets the due-by of a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim. Body {"dueBy":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. A due-by set this way stays as set (a holiday added later does not move it); overdue, the late charge, grace and the claim's period follow it; it may be before the claim's date. Refused with 422 for anyone but a steward, any other status, or a claim (or the new due-by) in a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/hold — toggles the hold on an OPEN or PENDING claim: holds it (CLAIM_HELD) or, when held, releases it (CLAIM_RELEASED). A held claim not bound by a statement counts in no live total, as a held person's claims do. Refused with 422 for any other status; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/lines — add a line to a DRAFT claim. Body {"label":"...","qty":"3","unit":"2.50"}. Adding a line edits the claim: its amount becomes its lines added up (quantity times unit amount) and the user is kept as its last editor. Refused with 422 for an empty label, a quantity that is not a whole number of at least 1, a unit amount not in up to two decimals, a claim that is not a draft, whose due-by is inside a closed period, or whose editor another user has open (locked); nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/lock — open the claim's editor: locks it for the user until they save or cancel it, or the sheet's today changes (releasing any other lock they hold on the sheet). 422 for a viewer, a claim that cannot be edited (not a draft, or dated inside a closed period) or one another user has locked; nothing is locked. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/person — a steward moves a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (body: {"personId": n}). It keeps its date, takes the next number of its sequence (a draft none), loses any figure a statement bound it to, and lists as its new person's newest claim. 422 for anything refused (not a steward, a settled or voided claim, a correction, no such person, a date after their retirement, or a claim dated inside a closed period); 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/proof — raise a claim's proofs count by one. The body may choose its kind, receipt or photo (none chosen: a receipt). Refused with 422 for a SETTLED or VOID claim, or a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId} — edit a claim's amount, date, note, the number it corrects and its reference. Body as for an add; refused the same way (400), 404 for a claim not on the sheet, and 422 for a claim that is not a draft, whose due-by (kept by the edit) is inside a closed period, whose editor another user has open (locked), or that has lines and is typed another amount than they add up to. Saving releases the user's lock on the claim. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/remind — remind an OPEN or PENDING claim: its reminded date becomes the sheet's today and REMIND is written. Refused with 422 for a claim in any other status, or one already reminded on the sheet's today; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. With an escalation gap set (escalate-after), a reminder at least that many days after the claim's previous one escalates it, once per claim ever: ESCALATE is written after REMIND. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/resettle — a steward re-freezes a SETTLED claim at the figure it would have today as an open claim bound by no statement. Refused with 422 for anyone else or any other status, and for a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/review-assign — a steward assigns a REVIEW claim's review to a user. Body {"user":"<user>"}. The claim shows the user from then on (kept after it leaves REVIEW) and REVIEW_ASSIGNED is written. Refused with 422 for anyone else, any other status, or a blank user; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/settle-part — part-settle an OPEN claim (body: {"amount":"5.25"}). The amount is split off as the split action does (CLAIM_SPLIT, CLAIM_OPENED, rollup lines), and the new claim is then settled by the user as the settle action does (CLAIM_SETTLED, or CLAIM_PENDING above the clerk limit; watchers; rollup lines). Four eyes and the proof rule are judged on the original claim; the new claim's opener is the user, who may still part-settle it. 422 when the split or the settle would be refused; nothing is stored or recorded. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. The step owns its transaction, so it is not governed here. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/shares — share a claim with another person on the sheet (body: {"personId":3,"share":"33.33"}): they hold that percent of its due, and CLAIM_SHARED is written. 422 for anything refused (the claim's own person, a person already holding a share, a share not more than 0.00, shares adding up to more than 100.00, or a SETTLED, VOID or DELETED claim); nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/split — split an amount off an OPEN claim (body: {"amount":"5.25"}). The claim keeps the rest of its amount and loses any figure a statement bound it to; a new OPEN claim with the split-off amount, the same date and note, the next number, opened by the user and due by its date plus the terms in force on it, is split from the claim's number and lists as the newest. 422 for anything refused (a role that may not open a claim, a claim not OPEN or deferred, an amount not more than 0.00 and less than the claim's, or a claim dated inside a closed period); nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/status/{status} — move a claim to OPEN, SETTLED, VOID or DELETED. A DRAFT claim can be DELETED (counting nowhere), and a DELETED one restored to DRAFT on the sheet's today it was deleted (CLAIM_RESTORED). DRAFT -> OPEN -> SETTLED, and DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING -> VOID; a steward may also void a SETTLED claim within 7 days of its settlement (the status log's SETTLED date) by the sheet's today. A clerk settling a claim above the clerk limit makes it PENDING; opening a DRAFT claim whose due-by falls in a period with a cap is refused (409) while its person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it, and so is opening one while its person already has the sheet's maximum of open claims (max-open) OPEN or PENDING; from PENDING a steward (not its opener) approves it (SETTLED) or rejects it (OPEN, with a "reason" in the body). Any other change is refused with 409 and nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet; 422 for a claim dated inside a closed period, or for a settle or approve of a claim with no proof whose due is above the proof threshold in force on its date, or for an open of a DRAFT claim with an empty note whose due is abo
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/timeline — the audit lines about the claim, newest first, exactly as the audit file holds them: those carrying number=<its number>, or for a claim with no number those naming its person, amount and date together. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/unlock — cancel the claim's editor: releases the user's lock on it, if they hold it. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/waive — a steward waives an OPEN or PENDING claim's late charge: it bears none from then on, whatever its overdue state, and CLAIM_WAIVED is written. Refused with 422 for anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet.

Body {"text":"..."}, lines of name,amount,date,note (a blank date is the entry date, else the sheet's today; the note may hold commas or be absent, and may end in " #<reference>": that part is the claim's reference, not its note). Responds {"adde
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/clone — a steward clones the sheet to another id. Body {"toSheetId":"..."}. The other sheet must never have been used. It gets this sheet's today, settings, roles, rates, retired grades, holidays, void reasons, templates, people (grades, terms, contacts, aliases, holds, retirements, patrons), pools, periods (all open) and claims (status, frozen figures, dates, notes, tags, references, logs), each numbered claim numbered afresh by the clone's own numbering in the order the originals were opened. Statements (and the figures they bound), watches, delegations, comments, locks and settle batches are not copied. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, no id, or a sheet already used. Responds with the id cloned to. 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/dashboard — the steward's dashboard for the user named by X-User: the PENDING and REVIEW claims and the overdue claims that count, over the sheet and all its descendants, each by its own today ({"pending":1,"review":0,"overdue":2}); every count null for a user who is not a steward on the sheet (as of the sheet's today, or the as-of date). 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations — the sheet's delegations of the steward role, in the order they were made. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations — a steward delegates the steward role to a user name. Body {"user":"wes","from":"yyyy-mm-dd","to":"yyyy-mm-dd"}, both dates inclusive; a blank from-date is the sheet's today, a blank to-date the from-date. Anyone but a steward, a blank user, a date that is not real, or a to-date before the from-date is refused with 400 and nothing is stored or recorded.

• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades — each grade of the sheet (A, B, C, then those added) and whether it is retired on the sheet ({grade, retired}).

Only a steward merges; the same grade twice, or a retired grade to merge into, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. A date that is not real, or one already on the list, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. Every claim not SETTLED or VOID due on or after the new holiday is due again by the terms-th business day after its date, with the terms it was fixed with, over the holidays now on the sheet; HOLIDAY_ADDED is followed by the rollup lines when any figure moved. 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/notes — the sheet's notes, newest first ({id, on, by, text}); as of a date, only those added while the sheet's today was on or before it. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/notes — adds a note to the sheet, dated the sheet's today. Body {"text":"..."}, trimmed. A blank text is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/openings/import — add opening balances per pasted line. Body {"text":"..."}, lines of name,period,amount (a person's name or alias on the sheet, ignoring case; a period on the sheet; an amount with two decimals, 0.00 or more). Every line is checked first: 400 for a bad line or none, and then nothing is stored. Otherwise each adds its amount to the person's opening balance for the period, part of their carried figure for it, in order (OPENING_SET). Responds {"set":n}, the lines that went through. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/import — add or update a person per pasted line. Body {"text":"..."}, lines of name,grade,terms,contact (the last two may be absent or blank; a blank grade is the sheet's default grade). A line whose name matches a person on the sheet (by name or alias) updates them as their edit form would (PERSON_EDITED); any other line adds one (PERSON_ADDED). Every line is checked first by the person form's rules: 400 for a bad line, a name or contact already in use, or one repeated in the import (ignoring case) — and then nothing is stored. Responds {"added":n,"updated":m}. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/approver — set the person's approver. Body {"user":"..."}; it replaces any approver they had (APPROVER_SET). The approver may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own). 400 for a blank user name, and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/claims — add a claim to a person. Body {"amount":"12.50","date":"yyyy-mm-dd","note":"...","corrects":"","ref":""}; a blank date is the entry date, else the sheet's today. An amount that is not a number with up to two decimals, a date that is not real, a negative amount (a correction) whose "corrects" is not the number of a SETTLED claim of the same person, or a "corrects" on an amount that is not negative, or a "ref" (trimmed; blank for none) another claim of the sheet already carries (ignoring case), is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet; 422 for a claim whose due-by (its date, or a blank date's today, plus its person's terms) is inside a closed period. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/flag — a steward flags the person. Body {"reason":"...","until":"yyyy-mm-dd"} (a blank until-date is the sheet's today); it replaces any flag they had (PERSON_FLAGGED). While the sheet's today is on or before the until-date, only a steward may open the person's claims. 400 for anyone but a steward, a blank reason or a date that is not real, and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/hold — add a hold to a person. Body {"from":"yyyy-mm-dd","to":"yyyy-mm-dd"}; a blank from-date is the sheet's today, a blank to-date has no end (a hold ends on its to-date). Their OPEN claims dated within a hold and not bound by a statement count in no live total. A date that is not real, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge — a steward merges the person into another on the sheet. Body {"intoId":123}. The merged person's claims move to the other (numbers and dates kept, each losing any figure a statement bound, listed after the other's in the order they were added); their name and aliases become the other's aliases; their patrons and pool memberships go to the other, and anyone naming them as patron names the other instead. Their statements, holds, watchers and contact are dropped and they leave the sheet. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, the same person, no such person, or either of them retired; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person merged into. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge-undo — the steward who made the last merge into the person undoes it, on the same sheet-today it was made: the merged person is back at the end of the list (their id, grades, terms, contact and tags as before) with the claims that came from them (their numbers and status as they are now) and their own aliases, which leave the person's; patron and pool changes stay. Records PERSON_MERGE_UNDONE, then the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines. 422, storing nothing, for anyone else, any later day, or a person with no merge to undo; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person restored. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/plans — add a plan to a person. Body {"amount":"10.00","start":"yyyy-mm-dd","every":"7","end":"yyyy-mm-dd"} (a blank date is the sheet's today). An amount the claim form would refuse, an interval that is not a whole number of at least 1, a bad date or an end before the start is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire — retire a person from a date. Body {"from":"yyyy-mm-dd"}; a blank date is the sheet's today. A date that is not real is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Retiring again moves the date. From the day it is reached, their open claims not bound by a statement count in no live total. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/statement — take a statement of a person: record their due-total now and bind each of their counting claims to its figure now. Body {"asOf":"yyyy-mm-dd"} takes it as of that date instead (blank: now): their claims and figures as they stood at the end of it. 404 for a person not on the sheet; 409 for a date that is not real, after the sheet's today, or before the person was on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/transfer — a steward transfers the person to another sheet by id. Body {"toSheetId":"..."}. The person arrives there with every grade they were given (and its from-date), their terms, contact and aliases, and their claims with their status, dates, notes, frozen figures, comments and logs; each numbered claim takes the next number of the other sheet, in the order the claims were opened (by the sheet's today when each was opened, then the order they were added). Figures a statement bound are lost (no statements go with them) and references are not carried. They leave this sheet entirely: patron links, pool memberships, holds, watches, plans and closed-period figures are dropped. When a person on the other sheet has their name or an alias of theirs (as names are compared), they are merged into that person there, as a merge does: their claims are listed after that person's, their name and aliases become that person's aliases, and their grades and contact are dropped; the other sheet records PERSON_TRANSFERRED then PERSON_MERGED. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, a retired person, no sheet id or this sheet's own, an archived s
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/transfer-undo — a steward undoes the transfer that brought the person to this sheet, on the same sheet-today they arrived: they are transferred back to the sheet they came from by exactly the transfer rules and lines (see transfer.POST.yml), then this sheet records PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE and its ROLLUP and TOTALS lines. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, a person who did not arrive by transfer, any later day, or anything a transfer refuses; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person as they arrived back. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unretire — unretire a retired person on the sheet's today. They are no longer retired; the retirement is kept as a past one, from its date to that day, and a claim dated strictly between the two is refused. Anyone not retired is refused with 409 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unstate — cancel a person's last statement: the claims it bound are live again. Steward only. 404 for a person not on the sheet; 409 for a user who is not a steward or a person with no statement. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-fy — make the twelve monthly periods of a fiscal year. Body {"year":"2026"}: fiscal year FY2026 starts on the first of the sheet's fiscal start month in 2026; each of its months is made as the period generator makes it (a month whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period is left out). A year that is not yyyy is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate — make a period per calendar month. Body {"from":"2026-02-15","to":"2026-04-10"}: one period per month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each from its first to its last day, named yyyy-mm. A month whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period on the sheet is left out. A bad date or a to-date before the from-date is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. A viewer changes nothing: they are told {"made":0}. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-quarters — make the four calendar quarters of a year. Body {"year":"2026"}: periods 2026-Q1 to 2026-Q4, from Jan-Mar to Oct-Dec; each is made as the period form adds it (a quarter whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period is left out). A year that is not yyyy is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods — the sheet's periods, by from-date. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/close — close a period, fixing its due-total (the figures of the counting claims dated in it) at this moment. 409 for a period not on the sheet or already closed. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/lock — lock a period. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already locked, or a user who is not a steward. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/reopen — reopen a closed period, making its due-total live again. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, not closed, or a user who is not a steward. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/soft-close — soft-close an open period, fixing its due-total (the figures of the counting claims dated in it) at this moment while its claims can still change. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already (soft-)closed, or a role not allowed to close. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/unlock — unlock a period. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already unlocked, or a user who is not a steward. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods — add a period. Body {"name":"P1","from":"2026-03-01","to":"2026-03-31","cap":"2"}: both dates inclusive; cap (blank: none) is how many OPEN or PENDING claims each person may have in it. A blank or taken name, a bad date, a to-date before the from-date, an overlap with another of the sheet's periods, or a cap that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover — roll fiscal year FY<yyyy> over. Body {"year":"2026"}. Only a steward (409 otherwise), and only for a year with a period (409 otherwise); a year that is not yyyy is 400. Nothing is stored when refused. Makes the next fiscal year's twelve months as the fiscal year generator does (PERIOD_ADDED), adds each person's open figure at the end of the old year's last period (their claims that count belonging to a period of the old year, OPEN or PENDING at its end) to their opening balance for the new year's first period (OPENING_SET), then records ROLLOVER fy=FY<yyyy> periods=<made>, then soft-closes every period of the old year still open, in start-date order (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED). Responds {"made":n}. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover-undo — undo the sheet's last rollover. Only the steward who made it, on the sheet-today it was made, once, and only while no claim belongs to a period it generated (409 otherwise; nothing is stored when refused). Removes the periods it generated, takes back the opening balances it set, then records ROLLOVER_UNDONE fy=FY<yyyy>. Responds {"fy":"FY<yyyy>","removed":n}. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/generate — for every plan of the sheet, in the order added, a DRAFT claim of its amount with an empty note for each plan date (the start, then every N days) up to its end and the sheet's today that it has made none for yet, by the claim form's rules: a date the form refuses is skipped and tried again next time. Responds {"made":n}. A viewer changes nothing: they are told {"made":0}. 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans — the sheet's plans, in the order added ({id, personId, amount, start, every, end, generated, day, nextDates, paused}), `generated` being how many claims the plan has made so far, `nextDates` its first five dates after the sheet's today and on or before its end that no pause skips, comma and space separated, and `paused` yes/no. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/amount — change a plan's amount (body {"amount":"20.00"}) on the sheet's today. The claims generated from then on are of the new amount; those it generated that are still DRAFT take it too, each as the claim editor would save it (CLAIM_EDITED, then ROLLUP/TOTALS for figures that moved); any other keeps its amount. An amount the claim form would refuse is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a plan not on the sheet. 
• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/pause — pause (body {"paused":true}) or resume ({"paused":false}) a plan on the sheet's today. A plan date on or after the day it was paused and before the day it was resumed is skipped. Pausing a paused plan or resuming a running one is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a plan not on the sheet. 
• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/pool-members — adds a person, or another pool, to a pool. Body {"pool":"...","personId":1,"share":"50.00"} or {"pool":"...","memberPool":"...","share":"50.00"}. A person already in the pool, a pool already a member of a pool, a pool containing itself through any chain, a chain more than three deep, or a share that is not more than 0.00 and at most 100.00 with at most two decimals, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/pools — the sheet's pools, in the order added, each with its members (in the order added), its total share (a retired member's share counting 0.00) and whether it is balanced (the total is exactly 100.00), and

1	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/archive — archive the sheet (no body). Only a steward may; anyone else, and an already archived sheet, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored. An archived sheet refuses every change. 
2	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/audit?name= — the sheet's audit lines exactly as the audit file holds them, newest first; with a name, only the lines carrying name=<it> or person=<it> (case and surrounding spaces ignored), followed by the matching lines of each of the sheet's descendants (sheets by id, each newest first), and when the name is (a name or alias of) a person transferred in, after them the lines about them on the sheet they came from (under the name they had there), newest first, as that sheet's file holds them. 
3	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/bulk-settle — settles the ticked claims all or nothing. Body {"claimIds":[...]}, in list order. Each is settled as settling it alone would (one going to PENDING counts as settled), in one transaction: if any is refused (or the user is a viewer, or the sheet archived), none is settled, all count as refused and nothing is stored or recorded. Otherwise they form the sheet's next settle batch, recorded after the claims' own lines as BATCH_SETTLED batch=<n> count=<claims> total=<their SETTLED frozen figures added up>. Responds {settled, refused, last}. The step owns its transaction, so it is not governed here. 
4	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/comments — comment on a claim. Body {"text":"..."}, kept trimmed with the user who wrote it and the sheet's today. Refused with 422 for an empty comment; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
5	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/date — a steward re-dates an OPEN or PENDING claim. Body {"date":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. Its due-by and any statement figure stay, and so its period (the one its due-by falls in) and its number. Refused with 422 for anyone but a steward, any other status, a date after its person's retirement, or a claim due by a date in a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
6	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/defer — defer an OPEN claim to a date after the sheet's today. Body {"until":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. Until the sheet's today reaches it the claim counts in no total, is not overdue, cannot be settled and is left unbound by a statement. Refused with 422 for a claim not OPEN, a date not after today, or a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
7	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/due-by — a steward sets the due-by of a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim. Body {"dueBy":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. A due-by set this way stays as set (a holiday added later does not move it); overdue, the late charge, grace and the claim's period follow it; it may be before the claim's date. Refused with 422 for anyone but a steward, any other status, or a claim (or the new due-by) in a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
8	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/hold — toggles the hold on an OPEN or PENDING claim: holds it (CLAIM_HELD) or, when held, releases it (CLAIM_RELEASED). A held claim not bound by a statement counts in no live total, as a held person's claims do. Refused with 422 for any other status; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
9	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/lines — add a line to a DRAFT claim. Body {"label":"...","qty":"3","unit":"2.50"}. Adding a line edits the claim: its amount becomes its lines added up (quantity times unit amount) and the user is kept as its last editor. Refused with 422 for an empty label, a quantity that is not a whole number of at least 1, a unit amount not in up to two decimals, a claim that is not a draft, whose due-by is inside a closed period, or whose editor another user has open (locked); nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
10	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/lock — open the claim's editor: locks it for the user until they save or cancel it, or the sheet's today changes (releasing any other lock they hold on the sheet). 422 for a viewer, a claim that cannot be edited (not a draft, or dated inside a closed period) or one another user has locked; nothing is locked. 
11	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/person — a steward moves a DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING claim to another person on the sheet (body: {"personId": n}). It keeps its date, takes the next number of its sequence (a draft none), loses any figure a statement bound it to, and lists as its new person's newest claim. 422 for anything refused (not a steward, a settled or voided claim, a correction, no such person, a date after their retirement, or a claim dated inside a closed period); 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
12	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/proof — raise a claim's proofs count by one. The body may choose its kind, receipt or photo (none chosen: a receipt). Refused with 422 for a SETTLED or VOID claim, or a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
13	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId} — edit a claim's amount, date, note, the number it corrects and its reference. Body as for an add; refused the same way (400), 404 for a claim not on the sheet, and 422 for a claim that is not a draft, whose due-by (kept by the edit) is inside a closed period, whose editor another user has open (locked), or that has lines and is typed another amount than they add up to. Saving releases the user's lock on the claim. 
14	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/remind — remind an OPEN or PENDING claim: its reminded date becomes the sheet's today and REMIND is written. Refused with 422 for a claim in any other status, or one already reminded on the sheet's today; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. With an escalation gap set (escalate-after), a reminder at least that many days after the claim's previous one escalates it, once per claim ever: ESCALATE is written after REMIND. 
15	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/resettle — a steward re-freezes a SETTLED claim at the figure it would have today as an open claim bound by no statement. Refused with 422 for anyone else or any other status, and for a claim dated inside a closed period; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
16	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/review-assign — a steward assigns a REVIEW claim's review to a user. Body {"user":"<user>"}. The claim shows the user from then on (kept after it leaves REVIEW) and REVIEW_ASSIGNED is written. Refused with 422 for anyone else, any other status, or a blank user; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
17	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/settle-part — part-settle an OPEN claim (body: {"amount":"5.25"}). The amount is split off as the split action does (CLAIM_SPLIT, CLAIM_OPENED, rollup lines), and the new claim is then settled by the user as the settle action does (CLAIM_SETTLED, or CLAIM_PENDING above the clerk limit; watchers; rollup lines). Four eyes and the proof rule are judged on the original claim; the new claim's opener is the user, who may still part-settle it. 422 when the split or the settle would be refused; nothing is stored or recorded. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. The step owns its transaction, so it is not governed here.

19	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/split — split an amount off an OPEN claim (body: {"amount":"5.25"}). The claim keeps the rest of its amount and loses any figure a statement bound it to; a new OPEN claim with the split-off amount, the same date and note, the next number, opened by the user and due by its date plus the terms in force on it, is split from the claim's number and lists as the newest. 422 for anything refused (a role that may not open a claim, a claim not OPEN or deferred, an amount not more than 0.00 and less than the claim's, or a claim dated inside a closed period); nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
20	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/status/{status} — move a claim to OPEN, SETTLED, VOID or DELETED. A DRAFT claim can be DELETED (counting nowhere), and a DELETED one restored to DRAFT on the sheet's today it was deleted (CLAIM_RESTORED). DRAFT -> OPEN -> SETTLED, and DRAFT, OPEN or PENDING -> VOID; a steward may also void a SETTLED claim within 7 days of its settlement (the status log's SETTLED date) by the sheet's today. A clerk settling a claim above the clerk limit makes it PENDING; opening a DRAFT claim whose due-by falls in a period with a cap is refused (409) while its person already has that many OPEN or PENDING claims in it, and so is opening one while its person already has the sheet's maximum of open claims (max-open) OPEN or PENDING; from PENDING a steward (not its opener) approves it (SETTLED) or rejects it (OPEN, with a "reason" in the body). Any other change is refused with 409 and nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet; 422 for a claim dated inside a closed period, or for a settle or approve of a claim with no proof whose due is above the proof threshold in force on its date, or for an open of a DRAFT claim with an empty note whose due is abo
21	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/timeline — the audit lines about the claim, newest first, exactly as the audit file holds them: those carrying number=<its number>, or for a claim with no number those naming its person, amount and date together. 404 for a claim not on the sheet. 
22	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/unlock — cancel the claim's editor: releases the user's lock on it, if they hold it. 
23	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/claims/{claimId}/waive — a steward waives an OPEN or PENDING claim's late charge: it bears none from then on, whatever its overdue state, and CLAIM_WAIVED is written. Refused with 422 for anyone else, any other status, or a claim already waived; nothing is stored. 404 for a claim not on the sheet.

Then, in paste order, each claim is added (or edited) and opened as its open button opens it (CLAIM_OPENED, then the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines), all in one transaction: any refusal the open button would give refuses the whole paste, and then nothing is stored or recorded. 25	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/clone — a steward clones the sheet to another id. Body {"toSheetId":"..."}. The other sheet must never have been used. It gets this sheet's today, settings, roles, rates, retired grades, holidays, void reasons, templates, people (grades, terms, contacts, aliases, holds, retirements, patrons), pools, periods (all open) and claims (status, frozen figures, dates, notes, tags, references, logs), each numbered claim numbered afresh by the clone's own numbering in the order the originals were opened. 26	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/dashboard — the steward's dashboard for the user named by X-User: the PENDING and REVIEW claims and the overdue claims that count, over the sheet and all its descendants, each by its own today ({"pending":1,"review":0,"overdue":2}); every count null for a user who is not a steward on the sheet (as of the sheet's today, or the as-of date). 
27	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations — the sheet's delegations of the steward role, in the order they were made. 
28	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/delegations — a steward delegates the steward role to a user name. Body {"user":"wes","from":"yyyy-mm-dd","to":"yyyy-mm-dd"}, both dates inclusive; a blank from-date is the sheet's today, a blank to-date the from-date. Anyone but a steward, a blank user, a date that is not real, or a to-date before the from-date is refused with 400 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
29	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/flags — every flag on the sheet's people ({personId, reason, until, shown}); shown is the reason while the sheet's today is on or before the until-date, else blank. 
30	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades — each grade of the sheet (A, B, C, then those added) and whether it is retired on the sheet ({grade, retired}). 
31	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/merge — merges a grade into another. Body {"from":"A|B|C","into":"A|B|C"}. Only a steward merges; the same grade twice, or a retired grade to merge into, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. Records GRADE_MERGED, then each person on the merged grade today is edited as the person form would, and (retroactively) every grade record of theirs on the merged grade becomes the other; then the ROLLUP lines for the merge as a whole. Responds with the grades and how many people were given the other grade. 
32	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/grades/retire — retires a grade on the sheet. Body {"grade":"A|B|C"}. Another grade, or one already retired, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. Responds with the grades, as GET grades does. 
33	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/holidays — adds a holiday to the sheet. Body {"date":"yyyy-mm-dd"}. A date that is not real, or one already on the list, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. Every claim not SETTLED or VOID due on or after the new holiday is due again by the terms-th business day after its date, with the terms it was fixed with, over the holidays now on the sheet; HOLIDAY_ADDED is followed by the rollup lines when any figure moved. 
34	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/notes — the sheet's notes, newest first ({id, on, by, text}); as of a date, only those added while the sheet's today was on or before it. 
35	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/notes — adds a note to the sheet, dated the sheet's today. Body {"text":"..."}, trimmed. A blank text is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
36	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/openings/import — add opening balances per pasted line. Body {"text":"..."}, lines of name,period,amount (a person's name or alias on the sheet, ignoring case; a period on the sheet; an amount with two decimals, 0.00 or more). Every line is checked first: 400 for a bad line or none, and then nothing is stored. Otherwise each adds its amount to the person's opening balance for the period, part of their carried figure for it, in order (OPENING_SET). Responds {"set":n}, the lines that went through. 
37	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/import — add or update a person per pasted line. Body {"text":"..."}, lines of name,grade,terms,contact (the last two may be absent or blank; a blank grade is the sheet's default grade). A line whose name matches a person on the sheet (by name or alias) updates them as their edit form would (PERSON_EDITED); any other line adds one (PERSON_ADDED). Every line is checked first by the person form's rules: 400 for a bad line, a name or contact already in use, or one repeated in the import (ignoring case) — and then nothing is stored. Responds {"added":n,"updated":m}. 
38	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/approver — set the person's approver. Body {"user":"..."}; it replaces any approver they had (APPROVER_SET). The approver may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own). 400 for a blank user name, and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
39	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/claims — add a claim to a person. Body {"amount":"12.50","date":"yyyy-mm-dd","note":"...","corrects":"","ref":""}; a blank date is the entry date, else the sheet's today. An amount that is not a number with up to two decimals, a date that is not real, a negative amount (a correction) whose "corrects" is not the number of a SETTLED claim of the same person, or a "corrects" on an amount that is not negative, or a "ref" (trimmed; blank for none) another claim of the sheet already carries (ignoring case), is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet; 422 for a claim whose due-by (its date, or a blank date's today, plus its person's terms) is inside a closed period. 
40	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/flag — a steward flags the person. Body {"reason":"...","until":"yyyy-mm-dd"} (a blank until-date is the sheet's today); it replaces any flag they had (PERSON_FLAGGED). While the sheet's today is on or before the until-date, only a steward may open the person's claims. 400 for anyone but a steward, a blank reason or a date that is not real, and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
41	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/hold — add a hold to a person. Body {"from":"yyyy-mm-dd","to":"yyyy-mm-dd"}; a blank from-date is the sheet's today, a blank to-date has no end (a hold ends on its to-date). Their OPEN claims dated within a hold and not bound by a statement count in no live total. A date that is not real, or a to-date before the from-date, is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
42	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge — a steward merges the person into another on the sheet. Body {"intoId":123}. The merged person's claims move to the other (numbers and dates kept, each losing any figure a statement bound, listed after the other's in the order they were added); their name and aliases become the other's aliases; their patrons and pool memberships go to the other, and anyone naming them as patron names the other instead. Their statements, holds, watchers and contact are dropped and they leave the sheet. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, the same person, no such person, or either of them retired; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person merged into. 
43	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/merge-undo — the steward who made the last merge into the person undoes it, on the same sheet-today it was made: the merged person is back at the end of the list (their id, grades, terms, contact and tags as before) with the claims that came from them (their numbers and status as they are now) and their own aliases, which leave the person's; patron and pool changes stay. Records PERSON_MERGE_UNDONE, then the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines. 422, storing nothing, for anyone else, any later day, or a person with no merge to undo; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person restored. 
44	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/plans — add a plan to a person. Body {"amount":"10.00","start":"yyyy-mm-dd","every":"7","end":"yyyy-mm-dd"} (a blank date is the sheet's today). An amount the claim form would refuse, an interval that is not a whole number of at least 1, a bad date or an end before the start is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
45	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/retire — retire a person from a date. Body {"from":"yyyy-mm-dd"}; a blank date is the sheet's today. A date that is not real is refused with 400 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Retiring again moves the date. From the day it is reached, their open claims not bound by a statement count in no live total. 
46	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/statement — take a statement of a person: record their due-total now and bind each of their counting claims to its figure now. Body {"asOf":"yyyy-mm-dd"} takes it as of that date instead (blank: now): their claims and figures as they stood at the end of it. 404 for a person not on the sheet; 409 for a date that is not real, after the sheet's today, or before the person was on the sheet. 
47	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/transfer — a steward transfers the person to another sheet by id. Body {"toSheetId":"..."}. The person arrives there with every grade they were given (and its from-date), their terms, contact and aliases, and their claims with their status, dates, notes, frozen figures, comments and logs; each numbered claim takes the next number of the other sheet, in the order the claims were opened (by the sheet's today when each was opened, then the order they were added). Figures a statement bound are lost (no statements go with them) and references are not carried. They leave this sheet entirely: patron links, pool memberships, holds, watches, plans and closed-period figures are dropped. When a person on the other sheet has their name or an alias of theirs (as names are compared), they are merged into that person there, as a merge does: their claims are listed after that person's, their name and aliases become that person's aliases, and their grades and contact are dropped; the other sheet records PERSON_TRANSFERRED then PERSON_MERGED. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, a retired person, no sheet id or this sheet's own, an archived s
48	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/transfer-undo — a steward undoes the transfer that brought the person to this sheet, on the same sheet-today they arrived: they are transferred back to the sheet they came from by exactly the transfer rules and lines (see transfer.POST.yml), then this sheet records PERSON_TRANSFER_UNDONE and its ROLLUP and TOTALS lines. 422, storing nothing, for anyone but a steward, a person who did not arrive by transfer, any later day, or anything a transfer refuses; 404 for a person not on the sheet. Responds with the person as they arrived back. 
49	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unretire — unretire a retired person on the sheet's today. They are no longer retired; the retirement is kept as a past one, from its date to that day, and a claim dated strictly between the two is refused. Anyone not retired is refused with 409 and nothing is stored; 404 for a person not on the sheet. 
50	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{personId}/unstate — cancel a person's last statement: the claims it bound are live again. Steward only. 404 for a person not on the sheet; 409 for a user who is not a steward or a person with no statement. 
51	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-fy — make the twelve monthly periods of a fiscal year. Body {"year":"2026"}: fiscal year FY2026 starts on the first of the sheet's fiscal start month in 2026; each of its months is made as the period generator makes it (a month whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period is left out). A year that is not yyyy is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. 
52	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate — make a period per calendar month. Body {"from":"2026-02-15","to":"2026-04-10"}: one period per month from the from-date's month to the to-date's month, each from its first to its last day, named yyyy-mm. A month whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period on the sheet is left out. A bad date or a to-date before the from-date is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. A viewer changes nothing: they are told {"made":0}. 
53	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-quarters — make the four calendar quarters of a year. Body {"year":"2026"}: periods 2026-Q1 to 2026-Q4, from Jan-Mar to Oct-Dec; each is made as the period form adds it (a quarter whose name is taken or whose days overlap a period is left out). A year that is not yyyy is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Responds {"made":n}. 
54	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods — the sheet's periods, by from-date. 
55	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/close — close a period, fixing its due-total (the figures of the counting claims dated in it) at this moment. 409 for a period not on the sheet or already closed. 
56	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/lock — lock a period. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already locked, or a user who is not a steward. 
57	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/reopen — reopen a closed period, making its due-total live again. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, not closed, or a user who is not a steward. 
58	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/soft-close — soft-close an open period, fixing its due-total (the figures of the counting claims dated in it) at this moment while its claims can still change. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already (soft-)closed, or a role not allowed to close. 
59	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/{name}/unlock — unlock a period. Steward only. 409 for a period not on the sheet, already unlocked, or a user who is not a steward. 
60	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods — add a period. Body {"name":"P1","from":"2026-03-01","to":"2026-03-31","cap":"2"}: both dates inclusive; cap (blank: none) is how many OPEN or PENDING claims each person may have in it. A blank or taken name, a bad date, a to-date before the from-date, an overlap with another of the sheet's periods, or a cap that is not a whole number of at least 1 is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. 
61	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover — roll fiscal year FY<yyyy> over. Body {"year":"2026"}. Only a steward (409 otherwise), and only for a year with a period (409 otherwise); a year that is not yyyy is 400. Nothing is stored when refused. Makes the next fiscal year's twelve months as the fiscal year generator does (PERIOD_ADDED), adds each person's open figure at the end of the old year's last period (their claims that count belonging to a period of the old year, OPEN or PENDING at its end) to their opening balance for the new year's first period (OPENING_SET), then records ROLLOVER fy=FY<yyyy> periods=<made>, then soft-closes every period of the old year still open, in start-date order (PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED). Responds {"made":n}. 
62	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/rollover-undo — undo the sheet's last rollover. Only the steward who made it, on the sheet-today it was made, once, and only while no claim belongs to a period it generated (409 otherwise; nothing is stored when refused). Removes the periods it generated, takes back the opening balances it set, then records ROLLOVER_UNDONE fy=FY<yyyy>. Responds {"fy":"FY<yyyy>","removed":n}. 
63	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/generate — for every plan of the sheet, in the order added, a DRAFT claim of its amount with an empty note for each plan date (the start, then every N days) up to its end and the sheet's today that it has made none for yet, by the claim form's rules: a date the form refuses is skipped and tried again next time. Responds {"made":n}. A viewer changes nothing: they are told {"made":0}. 
64	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans — the sheet's plans, in the order added ({id, personId, amount, start, every, end, generated, day, nextDates, paused}), `generated` being how many claims the plan has made so far, `nextDates` its first five dates after the sheet's today and on or before its end that no pause skips, comma and space separated, and `paused` yes/no. 
65	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/amount — change a plan's amount (body {"amount":"20.00"}) on the sheet's today. The claims generated from then on are of the new amount; those it generated that are still DRAFT take it too, each as the claim editor would save it (CLAIM_EDITED, then ROLLUP/TOTALS for figures that moved); any other keeps its amount. An amount the claim form would refuse is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a plan not on the sheet. 
66	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/plans/{planId}/pause — pause (body {"paused":true}) or resume ({"paused":false}) a plan on the sheet's today. A plan date on or after the day it was paused and before the day it was resumed is skipped. Pausing a paused plan or resuming a running one is refused with 422 and nothing is stored; 404 for a plan not on the sheet. 
67	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/pool-members — adds a person, or another pool, to a pool. Body {"pool":"...","personId":1,"share":"50.00"} or {"pool":"...","memberPool":"...","share":"50.00"}. A person already in the pool, a pool already a member of a pool, a pool containing itself through any chain, a chain more than three deep, or a share that is not more than 0.00 and at most 100.00 with at most two decimals, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
68	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/pools — the sheet's pools, in the order added, each with its members (in the order added), its total share (a retired member's share counting 0.00) and whether it is balanced (the total is exactly 100.00), and each member's cut of the sheet's pot when the pool is balanced and there is a pot (a member held on the sheet's today has none, their share spread over the members with a cut), and its cut as it stood at the end of each period whose to-date is on or before the sheet's today (read from the store as of that to-date). 
69	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/pools — adds a pool. Body {"name":"..."}, trimmed. A blank name, or one already a pool of the sheet, is refused with 422 and nothing is stored or recorded. 
70	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/quick — quick-add a DRAFT claim by name. Body {"name":"...","amount":"12.50"}. The claim is dated the entry date (else the sheet's today) with an empty note; a name not on the sheet (ignoring case) adds that person first, with the sheet's default grade (A when none is set). Refused as the person and claim forms are — 400 for a blank name or a bad amount, 422 for a claim whose due-by (its date plus the terms it would get) is inside a closed period — before anything is stored or recorded. 
71	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/rates — the sheet's rates, by grade, then by from-date, with level 0; then its parent's with level 1, and so on up to three levels up. 
72	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/rates/{grade} — set the grade's rate. Body {"rate":"12.50","from":"2026-03-05","to":"2026-03-31"}: from is optional (blank: from the beginning of time); a rate with the same grade and from is kept as an older version and this one added as the newest (the response carries its version); to is optional (blank: no end) and a to before the from is refused. A percent of 0.00 or more with up to two decimals. Another grade or a bad rate is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. 
73	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/rates/{grade}/withdraw — withdraw the grade's rate for a from-date. Body {"from":"2026-03-05"} (blank: the rate from the beginning of time). Steward only. The newest version is removed and the one before it, when there is one, applies again; with none before it the rate is gone (RATE_WITHDRAWN, then its ROLLUP lines). A user who is not a steward, or a grade and from-date with no rate, is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. 
74	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/rates/import — set a rate per pasted line. Body {"text":"..."}, lines of grade,rate,from,to (the last two may be absent or blank). Every line is checked first by the rate form's rules: 400 for a bad line or none, and then nothing is stored. Otherwise each is set in order as the form sets it (replacing a rate for the same grade and from-date; RATE_SET, then its ROLLUP lines). Responds {"set":n}. 
75	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/roles — the roles the sheet gives user names, by name. A name not listed is a clerk. 
76	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/roles/{user} — give the user name a role. Body {"role":"steward"}: clerk, steward or viewer (sees everything, changes nothing); anything else is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. 
77	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/search?text= — every person on the sheet's tree whose name or an alias contains the text (case ignored; empty matches everyone), one line each as "<sheet id> <name> <due-total>": this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by sheet id. 
78	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/settings — the sheet's settings in force on its today: {"clerkLimit":"1.50","floor":"1.00","terms":"14",...} ("" for no limit), and "dated": every value recorded for each dated setting, by key: [{"from":"2026-03-05","value":"5.00"}]. 
79	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/settings — save the sheet's settings. Body {"clerkLimit":"1.50","floor":"1.00","terms":"14","latePct":"0.00"}: amounts and the late percent with up to two decimals, kept with two; terms a whole number of days. A blank clerk limit is no limit (left as it is when a floor, terms or late percent are saved with it); a blank or missing floor, terms or late percent is left as it is. "policyDate" and "periodNumberingFrom" are yyyy-mm-dd dates: missing is left as it is, blank is none (off). "cap" is an amount with up to two decimals, kept with two: missing is left as it is, blank is none. Anything else is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. Every saved setting is audited, even the value already in force, then the ROLLUP and TOTALS lines of the figures the floor moved. "from" gives, by setting key, the from-date (yyyy-mm-dd) a dated setting (clerk-limit, floor, terms, terms-<grade>, late-pct, cap) is recorded from; blank or missing: the sheet's today. A value already recorded from that date is replaced. 
80	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/settle-batches — the number of the sheet's last settle batch ({last}, null for none). 
81	• POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/settle-batches — records a bulk settle as the sheet's next batch. Body {"claimIds":[...]}: the claims it settled; those on the sheet now SETTLED or PENDING carry the batch's number. With none, no batch is made. Responds with the sheet's last batch number ({last}, null for none). 
82	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/snapshots/compare?from=&to= — per person in list order, "<name> <then> <now>": then is the due-total of the SNAPSHOT written when the sheet's today was changed away from the from-date (blank: the sheet's today), now likewise for the to-date, or the person's due-total now when the to-date is blank. A figure with no snapshot is empty; each line is trimmed. 
83	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/statements — per person with a statement: the count, and the last one's due-total and date. 
84	• PUT /api/sheets/{sheetId}/today — change the sheet's today. Body {"today":"yyyy-mm-dd"}; blank is the real date. A date that is not real is refused with 400 and nothing is stored. With grace days set, each open period whose to-date plus the grace days is before the new today is then closed (PERIOD_CLOSED ... auto=yes). A role the permission matrix does not allow to change today (perm-today) is refused with 422. Every claim's lock on the sheet is released. Before any period closes, one SNAPSHOT per person (list order) records the due-total as it stood on the day being left; while the score log is on, one SCORE per person (list order) before them records the score as it stood then. 
85	• GET /api/sheets/{sheetId}/tree-people — every person on the sheet's tree as [sheet id, name, grade, due-total]: this sheet's people first in list order, then the other sheets' by sheet id.
